newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up on Friday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) but profit-taking pushed prices off highs, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,420 yuan ($2,823) per tonne, rising 70 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,650 and hit a low of 23,400.
March rose 90 yuan to 23,280, April 130 to 23,380, May 100 to 23,430, July 100 to 23,450 and August 210 to 23,500.
Combined volume fell to 40,090 tonnes from 57,860.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices down to end at or near their intraday lows, still up from Thursday's close.
Traders said investors liquidated their positions because they were not certain about the direction the LME will take.
"If LME copper cannot breach the $2,410 level on Friday, copper on the Shanghai market is likely to go through a correction early next week," said one analyst.
Traders said they expected copper to move in a narrow range early next week on market uncertainties.
